Dasgupta, 2021: The Economics of Biodiversity: The Dasgupta Review, HM Treasury

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of the structure and limits of general equilibrium theory

Mas-Colell, 1985: The Theory of General Economic Equilibrium: A Differentiable Approach, Cambridge University Press

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of constrained inefficiency of equilibria with incomplete markets
key_works: Geanakoplos and Polemarchakis, 1986: Existence, Regularity, and Constrained Suboptimality of Competitive Allocations when the Asset Market Is Incomplete, in Essays in Honor of Kenneth Arrow
nominations.rationale: Their result shows a generic scope for welfare-improving intervention when markets are incomplete. It underlies modern macroprudential and pecuniary-externality analysis. The policy translation came through later work by others.

nominations.contribution: for the discovery of sunspot equilibria and extrinsic uncertainty in dynamic economies

Cass and Shell, 1983: Do Sunspots Matter?, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: They showed that beliefs alone can drive equilibrium fluctuations, a lasting idea in macro and finance. The result is formally clean. It has had limited quantitative traction, and David Cass is deceased.

nominations.contribution: for the theory of equality of opportunity and fairness in normative economics
key_works: Roemer, 1998: Equality of Opportunity, Harvard University Press
Fleurbaey, 2008: Fairness, Responsibility, and Welfare, Oxford University Press
nominations.rationale: They gave operational normative criteria now used to evaluate redistribution and mobility. These criteria are relevant for judging welfare-state policy. The reservation is closeness to Sen's 1998 prize.

nominations.contribution: for the axiomatic theory of fair allocation and cost sharing
key_works: Moulin, 1988: Axioms of Cooperative Decision Making, Cambridge University Press
Moulin, 2003: Fair Division and Collective Welfare, MIT Press
Thomson, 2011: Fair allocation rules, Handbook of Social Choice and Welfare
nominations.rationale: These works map precisely which fairness, efficiency and incentive properties are compatible. That underpins much of practical market design. The main reservation is that the work is less visible outside theory.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of the structure and regularity of general equilibrium
key_works: Sonnenschein, 1973: Do Walras' identity and continuity characterize the class of community excess demand functions?, Journal of Economic Theory
Mas-Colell, 1985: The Theory of General Economic Equilibrium: A Differentiable Approach, Cambridge University Press
nominations.rationale: The Sonnenschein-Mantel-Debreu result is a fundamental impossibility frontier for aggregation. Debreu's 1983 prize partly overlaps with it.

nominations.contribution: for the theory and measurement of equality of opportunity
key_works: Roemer, 1998: Equality of Opportunity, Harvard University Press
Fleurbaey, 2008: Fairness, Responsibility, and Welfare, Oxford University Press
nominations.rationale: This is a normative framework that separates responsibility from circumstance, with clear axiomatic trade-offs. It may be seen as close to Sen's prize.

nominations.contribution: for showing the generic constrained inefficiency of incomplete-market equilibria
key_works: Geanakoplos and Polemarchakis, 1986: Existence, regularity, and constrained suboptimality of competitive allocations when the asset market is incomplete, in Essays in Honor of Kenneth Arrow
nominations.rationale: This is a deep and clean welfare result with implications for regulation. Its institutional impact is indirect.

Foster, Greer and Thorbecke, 1984: A class of decomposable poverty measures, Econometrica

nominations.contribution: for the measurement of poverty and inequality

people.affiliation: George Washington University and University of Oxford

key_works: Foster, Greer and Thorbecke, 1984: A class of decomposable poverty measures, Econometrica
Alkire and Foster, 2011: Counting and multidimensional poverty measurement, Journal of Public Economics
Foster, 2011: Freedom, opportunity, and well-being, in Handbook of Social Choice and Welfare
nominations.rationale: This work made poverty and deprivation measurement axiomatic, decomposable and usable by governments and international organizations. It is a clear example of welfare economics becoming a practical measurement technology. The reservation is that part of the decisive FGT contribution includes coauthors who are no longer prize-eligible.

nominations.contribution: for the theory of strategy-proof social choice
key_works: Gibbard, 1973: Manipulation of voting schemes: A general result, Econometrica
Satterthwaite, 1975: Strategy-proofness and Arrow’s conditions: Existence and correspondence theorems for voting procedures and social welfare functions, Journal of Economic Theory
Gibbard, 1977: Manipulation of schemes that mix voting with chance, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: The Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem is a central impossibility result showing the tension between collective choice and incentives. It is foundational for later mechanism design and voting theory. The reservation is classification, since the contribution straddles social choice, public choice and game theory.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to welfare economics, the evaluation of natural capital, and intergenerational equity
key_works: Dasgupta, 2021: The Economics of Biodiversity: The Dasgupta Review, HM Treasury
Arrow, Dasgupta, Goulder, et al., 2004: Are We Consuming Too Much?, Journal of Economic Perspectives
nominations.rationale: Dasgupta's rigorous extensions of welfare economics to intertemporal resource allocation provide the definitive foundation for evaluating environmental policy. His approach perfectly balances deep normative criteria with the complex dynamic general equilibrium of the natural world. It is the theoretical backbone for integrated assessment of climate and biodiversity.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to the computational and mathematical methods used to solve dynamic general equilibrium models
key_works: Judd, 1998: Numerical Methods in Economics, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: Judd brought advanced computational and numerical optimization methods into dynamic general equilibrium, enabling the solution of complex, heterogeneous macro models. His methodological rigor paved the way for modern quantitative policy evaluation. Without these numerical tools, modern climate-macro and structural tax policy models would be unsolvable.

nominations.contribution: for his analysis of general equilibrium with incomplete markets and the macroeconomic consequences of leverage
key_works: Geanakoplos, 1990: An Introduction to General Equilibrium with Incomplete Markets, Journal of Mathematical Economics
Geanakoplos, 2010: The Leverage Cycle, NBER Macroeconomics Annual
nominations.rationale: He fundamentally advanced the general equilibrium theory of incomplete markets, demonstrating how endogenous leverage margins drive systemic risk. The framework elegantly proves that competitive equilibria can be robustly inefficient when collateral constraints bind. This insight bridges pure equilibrium theory with urgent macroeconomic realities.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to the theory of social and economic networks and their general equilibrium implications
key_works: Jackson and Wolinsky, 1996: A Strategic Model of Social and Economic Networks, Journal of Economic Theory
nominations.rationale: Jackson developed the tractable theoretical framework required to model endogenous network formation in economic systems. His work details how decentralized interaction maps into aggregate welfare and systemic resilience. It expands the traditional general equilibrium paradigm to incorporate realistic connectivity and externalities.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to welfare economics, the measurement of social progress, and the incorporation of equity into economic policy
key_works: Fleurbaey, 2009: Beyond GDP: The Quest for a Measure of Social Welfare, Journal of Economic Literature
nominations.rationale: Fleurbaey has rigorously defined how to aggregate multidimensional individual well-being into coherent social welfare functions. His work provides the axiomatic structure needed to incorporate fairness and equity into formal policy evaluation. This is highly valuable when navigating the complex distributional impacts of long-horizon problems like climate change.

name: Tommy Andersson

nominations.contribution: for their axiomatic analysis of fair allocation and strategy-proof mechanisms
key_works: Moulin, H., 1988: Axioms of Cooperative Decision Making, Cambridge University Press
Thomson, W., 2011: Fair Allocation Rules, Handbook of Social Choice and Welfare
nominations.rationale: They established the axiomatic possibility and impossibility frontiers for fairness, stability, and strategy-proofness. Their clean, theoretically deep results directly inform practical mechanism design in environments where prices are unavailable, precisely aligning with my own core research values.

nominations.contribution: for the conceptualization of envy-freeness and its application to the theory of fair resource allocation
key_works: Foley, D. K., 1967: Resource allocation and the public sector, Yale Economic Essays
Varian, H. R., 1974: Equity, envy, and efficiency, Journal of Economic Theory
nominations.rationale: They formalized the concept of envy-freeness, a cornerstone of modern normative allocation. This benchmark is absolutely indispensable for designing practical matching markets, though their original focus on divisible goods requires extension for the indivisibility problem.

nominations.contribution: for their contributions to normative welfare economics and the formalization of equality of opportunity
key_works: Roemer, J. E., 1998: Equality of Opportunity, Harvard University Press
nominations.rationale: They rigorously formalized equality of opportunity, providing axiomatic characterizations of fair allocation that respect individual responsibility. Their deep normative theory defines precise bounds for evaluating public-sector distributional goals.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to the theory of fair division and the evolution of social institutions
key_works: Young, H. P., 1994: Equity: In Theory and Practice, Princeton University Press
nominations.rationale: His application of axiomatic analysis to fair division provides mathematically robust solutions for real-world allocation problems like taxation and representation. He successfully bridges pure theory and implementable fairness algorithms.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to welfare economics, particularly regarding population, environmental limits, and intergenerational equity
key_works: Dasgupta, P., 2001: Human Well-Being and the Natural Environment, Oxford University Press
nominations.rationale: His normative analysis extends formal welfare economics into the vital domains of environmental limits and population ethics. It represents a conceptually deep application of equilibrium constraints to long-run intergenerational allocation.

nominations.contribution: for the empirical and experimental analysis of social preferences and their implications for economic welfare
key_works: Fehr and Schmidt, 1999: A Theory of Fairness, Competition, and Cooperation, Quarterly Journal of Economics
Fehr and Gachter, 2000: Cooperation and Punishment in Public Goods Experiments, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: This contribution used highly controlled, replicable lab and field experiments to prove that fairness and reciprocity fundamentally alter economic equilibrium and welfare. It exemplifies how rigorous experimental measurement can overturn classical assumptions, yielding robust and economically meaningful effect sizes that have been independently replicated hundreds of times. This work successfully grounds welfare theory in actual human behavior.

nominations.contribution: for incorporating psychological realism into economic theory and welfare economics
key_works: Rabin, 1993: Incorporating Fairness into Game Theory and Economics, American Economic Review
O'Donoghue and Rabin, 1999: Doing It Now or Later, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: By mathematically formalizing robust experimental insights into fairness and time inconsistency, this work provided theorists with falsifiable models of bounded rationality. It translates replicable behavioral effects into precise equilibrium concepts that can be tested in large datasets. A reservation might be whether behavioral parameters are sufficiently stable across contexts for reliable general welfare calculation.

nominations.contribution: for the axiomatic approach to inequality measurement and the evaluation of social welfare
key_works: Bourguignon, 1979: Decomposable Income Inequality Measures, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: This research provided the mathematical foundations for rigorously and consistently measuring inequality and poverty in empirical data. By establishing metrics that are decomposable and robust, it allowed applied researchers worldwide to evaluate welfare changes with confidence and transparency. It fundamentally improved how economists process and evaluate distributional evidence.

nominations.contribution: for the formulation of equality of opportunity and its application to welfare economics
key_works: Roemer, 1998: Equality of Opportunity, Harvard University Press
nominations.rationale: This theoretical work provides a rigorous framework for separating outcomes derived from individual effort from those caused by circumstances, profoundly shaping normative economics. The framework has catalyzed a large empirical literature attempting to measure inequality of opportunity robustly. The empirical challenge remains correctly identifying and measuring the full set of unobserved circumstances.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of learning dynamics and the evolution of social conventions in equilibrium
key_works: Young, 1993: The Evolution of Conventions, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: This work uses evolutionary game theory to explain how stable equilibria and welfare-enhancing norms emerge from the decentralized learning of boundedly rational agents. The theoretical predictions regarding convergence and equilibrium selection have been subjected to rigorous testing in experimental economics. It provides a robust, testable bridge between formal equilibrium theory and observable social behavior.

nominations.contribution: for their empirical analysis of long-run trends in economic inequality
key_works: Piketty and Saez, 2003: Income Inequality in the United States, 1913-1998, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: By pioneering the extraction of top income shares from long-run historical tax registers, they revolutionized the measurement of inequality and welfare. Their work demonstrates the unparalleled value of administrative records in capturing long-run economic dynamics.

nominations.contribution: for his empirical analysis of consumer behavior, labor supply, and welfare reform
key_works: Blundell and MaCurdy, 1999: Labor Supply: A Review of Alternative Approaches, Handbook of Labor Economics
nominations.rationale: He seamlessly integrates quasi-experimental evaluation of policy with structural models of life-cycle labor supply. This careful methodological synthesis permits robust welfare conclusions regarding taxation and social transfers.

nominations.contribution: for his formulation of the theory of equality of opportunity
key_works: Roemer, 1998: Equality of Opportunity, Harvard University Press
nominations.rationale: He provides a rigorous normative framework for separating the impacts of individual effort from the circumstances of social background. This theoretical structure is essential for evaluating welfare-state institutions, education rules, and long-run mobility.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to welfare economics and the measurement of inclusive wealth
key_works: Dasgupta and Mäler, 2000: Net National Product, Wealth, and Social Well-Being, Environment and Development Economics
nominations.rationale: He mathematically extended general equilibrium and welfare theory to incorporate natural capital and environmental externalities. His framework guides the appropriate evaluation of sustainable economic progress and long-run intergenerational welfare.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to the measurement of poverty, inequality, and economic welfare
key_works: Bourguignon, 1979: Decomposable Income Inequality Measures, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: His development of robust axiomatic measures of inequality allows researchers to systematically decompose welfare differences across groups. These tools are indispensable for the empirical evaluation of distributional outcomes in policy analysis.

nominations.contribution: for the empirical analysis of the distribution of income and wealth
key_works: Piketty and Saez, 2003: Income Inequality in the United States, 1913-1998, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: They transformed normative welfare economics by compiling exhaustive, granular tax records. Strömberg heavily respects how new, rigorous micro-data is used here to pry open the 'black box' of long-run capital allocation and inequality.

nominations.contribution: for the theory of general equilibrium with incomplete markets and idiosyncratic risk
key_works: Bewley, 1986: Equilibrium with a Continuum of Independent Consumers
nominations.rationale: By incorporating critical frictions like incomplete markets into general equilibrium, this framework shares theoretical parallels with the incomplete contracting environments that define corporate finance.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of social and economic networks and their role in resource allocation
key_works: Jackson and Wolinsky, 1996: A Strategic Model of Social and Economic Networks, Journal of Economic Theory
nominations.rationale: Networks serve as the granular institutional structures that constrain market equilibrium behavior, capturing the relational frictions that purely anonymous markets miss.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to welfare economics and the valuation of natural capital
key_works: Dasgupta and Heal, 1979: Economic Theory and Exhaustible Resources, Cambridge University Press
nominations.rationale: His work extends formal welfare frameworks to account for physical constraints and institutional sustainability, connecting theory with the actual depletion of real assets.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to the theories of distributive justice and equality of opportunity
key_works: Roemer, 1998: Equality of Opportunity, Harvard University Press
nominations.rationale: Roemer rigorously models the institutional constraints and initial endowments that generate social disparities, offering a sharp mechanistic perspective on welfare criteria.

nominations.contribution: for their development of applied general equilibrium models and their application to public policy and international trade
key_works: Shoven and Whalley, 1984: Applied general-equilibrium models of taxation and international trade: An introduction and survey, Journal of Economic Literature
nominations.rationale: They pioneered computable general-equilibrium analysis, transforming the abstract Walrasian system into quantitative models calibrated to real-world national accounts. Their structural methodology laid the foundational quantitative framework for modern macroeconomic evaluation. A common reservation is that CGE outcomes are highly sensitive to initial calibration and assumed elasticities.

nominations.contribution: for his analysis of market demand and exact aggregation in general equilibrium theory
key_works: Hildenbrand, 1983: On the 'Law of Demand', Econometrica
nominations.rationale: His rigorous mathematical analysis established conditions under which aggregate market demand behaves predictably, even when individual behavior does not. I highly value his focus on the shape of income distributions to ensure stable macroeconomic regularities from complex micro foundations. The main reservation is the technical abstraction required to establish these general proofs.

nominations.contribution: for his fundamental contributions to microeconomic theory and the rigorous formulation of general equilibrium
key_works: Mas-Colell, 1985: The Theory of General Economic Equilibrium: A Differentiable Approach, Cambridge University Press
nominations.rationale: He advanced the rigorous mathematical formulation of general equilibrium, significantly expanding its flexibility and applicability. His work provides the absolute theoretical bedrock upon which all modern calibrated structural models rely. His contributions are heavily theoretical, sometimes detached from direct empirical quantification.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to welfare economics and the integration of environmental resources into economic measurement
key_works: Dasgupta and Heal, 1974: The optimal depletion of exhaustible resources, Review of Economic Studies
nominations.rationale: He pioneered the integration of environmental and natural capital into normative growth theory and long-run welfare accounting. This structural approach to sustainability provides a disciplined, general-equilibrium method to correct long-standing measurement errors in national accounts. The challenge remains the severe data constraints in cleanly valuing natural capital.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to welfare economics and the formalization of equality of opportunity
key_works: Roemer, 1998: Equality of Opportunity, Harvard University Press
nominations.rationale: He formalized the concept of equality of opportunity, separating outcomes into those driven by individual effort versus external circumstances. This offers a rigorous normative framework for evaluating distributional dynamics and inequality within growth models. A reservation is the practical difficulty of empirically isolating effort from unobservable circumstances.

nominations.contribution: for the development of general equilibrium models with heterogeneous agents, incomplete markets, and idiosyncratic risk
key_works: Bewley, 1977: The Permanent Income Hypothesis: A Theoretical Formulation, Journal of Economic Theory
nominations.rationale: His foundational models allow researchers to rigorously map macroeconomic shocks onto distributional consequences. In a field concerned with inequality, tracking heterogeneous historical responses within an equilibrium framework is indispensable.

nominations.contribution: for the formalization of equality of opportunity and its application to distributive justice and welfare economics
key_works: Roemer, 1998: Equality of Opportunity, Harvard University Press
nominations.rationale: His theoretical framework for isolating circumstances beyond an individual's control provides a robust normative basis for measuring intergenerational and spatial inequality. It ensures that the measurement of regional disparity is tied to deep mechanisms of justice.

nominations.contribution: for contributions to welfare economics, particularly concerning the environment, population, and intergenerational well-being
key_works: Dasgupta and Heal, 1979: Economic Theory and Exhaustible Resources, Cambridge University Press
nominations.rationale: By extending welfare criteria across long time horizons and integrating natural capital, he ensures that economic theory aligns with the physical realities of long-run survival. His work embodies the long-horizon viewpoint essential to historical analysis.

nominations.contribution: for the integration of fairness and social choice theory into the measurement of welfare and living standards
key_works: Fleurbaey, 2008: Fairness, Responsibility, and Welfare, Oxford University Press
nominations.rationale: His rigorous normative criteria for evaluating social progress provide a sophisticated theoretical counterpart to the empirical measurement of long-run inequality. He translates abstract welfare propositions into measurable tools.

nominations.contribution: for contributions to mechanism design, social choice, and the axiomatic theory of fair division
key_works: Moulin, 2003: Fair Division and Collective Welfare, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: His axiomatic approach offers precise, durable mathematical tools for understanding how scarce resources can be allocated equitably. This foundational work on fairness translates robustly across widely varying institutional contexts.

name: Richard Friberg

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to the measurement and analysis of historical wealth and income inequality
key_works: Piketty, 2003: Income Inequality in France, 1901-1998, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: He fundamentally revolutionized the empirical measurement of inequality by systematically exploiting long-run tax records. His work established an entirely new factual baseline for welfare and distributional theories.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to welfare economics, particularly regarding population, resources, and sustainable development
key_works: Dasgupta and Heal, 1979: Economic Theory and Exhaustible Resources, Cambridge University Press
nominations.rationale: He expanded the boundaries of welfare economics by rigorously integrating natural capital, biodiversity, and population dynamics into theoretical models. His frameworks allow for the precise evaluation of intergenerational equity.

nominations.contribution: for his foundational analysis of social and economic networks and their implications for welfare
key_works: Jackson and Wolinsky, 1996: A Strategic Model of Social and Economic Networks, Journal of Economic Theory
nominations.rationale: He established the formal theoretical apparatus for understanding how decentralized economic agents form networks. His work provides vital micro-foundations for understanding systemic risk, information diffusion, and market failures.

nominations.contribution: for their pioneering contributions to the development and application of computable general equilibrium models
key_works: Shoven and Whalley, 1984: Applied General-Equilibrium Models of Taxation and International Trade, Journal of Economic Literature
nominations.rationale: They successfully operationalized abstract general equilibrium theory by developing computable numerical models. This allowed policymakers to quantify the highly complex welfare impacts of taxes, trade policies, and economic integration.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to welfare economics and social choice, particularly the integration of responsibility into theories of fairness
key_works: Fleurbaey, 2008: Fairness, Responsibility, and Welfare, Oxford University Press
nominations.rationale: He translated abstract philosophical concepts of egalitarianism and responsibility into precise, axiomatic economic models. This provides a rigorous analytical foundation for designing equitable public policies.

nominations.contribution: for their contributions to welfare economics and the formalization of equality of opportunity
key_works: Roemer, 1998: Equality of Opportunity, Harvard UP
Fleurbaey, 2008: Fairness, Responsibility, and Welfare, Oxford UP
nominations.rationale: They formalized the crucial distinction between circumstances outside an individual's control and personal effort, providing a normative framework for equality of opportunity. This structural understanding of fairness is essential for evaluating the intergenerational persistence of inequality and institutional discrimination.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to welfare economics and the analysis of social capital and environmental resources
key_works: Dasgupta, 2001: Human Well-Being and the Natural Environment, OUP
nominations.rationale: She would appreciate his broad, institutional view of welfare that incorporates the long-run sustainability of natural resources, social capital, and health into formal economic measurement. His work emphasizes the deep structural interdependencies that govern societal well-being over generations.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to normative policy analysis and welfare evaluation under uncertainty
key_works: Manski, 2013: Public Policy in an Uncertain World, Harvard UP
nominations.rationale: His methodological work on partial identification directly tackles the limits of causal inference, forcing empirical researchers to be transparent about what can actually be learned from observational data. This rigorous standard for policy evaluation is highly relevant to the careful empirical study of criminal justice and social programs.

nominations.contribution: for his analysis of fair division and cooperative welfare economics
key_works: Moulin, 2003: Fair Division and Collective Welfare, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: His axiomatic approach to fair division mathematically formalizes how institutional rules can be designed to achieve equitable outcomes in resource allocation. This focus on the explicit design of rules to mitigate inequality speaks directly to her interest in institutional mechanisms.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to the theory of institutional evolution and welfare distribution
key_works: Young, 1993: The Evolution of Conventions, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: His evolutionary models of social conventions provide profound insight into how historical institutions and norms form, persist, and govern human behavior over long time horizons. This theoretical foundation bridges the gap between historical data analysis and modern institutional economics.

nominations.contribution: for the integration of equality of opportunity and political economy into welfare economics
key_works: Roemer, 1998: Equality of Opportunity, Harvard University Press
nominations.rationale: His axiomatic approach clearly distinguishes between outcomes derived from structural circumstances and those from individual effort, mirroring debates on impartial administration. The conceptual clarity is outstanding, though empirically operationalizing these bounds across different comparative institutional settings remains a challenge.

nominations.contribution: for the axiomatic analysis of fair allocation and the measurement of social welfare beyond GDP
key_works: Fleurbaey, 2008: Fairness, Responsibility, and Welfare, Oxford University Press
nominations.rationale: He provides explicit aggregation models that translate abstract concepts of fairness and multidimensional well-being into measurable public indicators. This work enables cumulative interdisciplinary research into how different political regimes generate social welfare, although building consensus on the underlying normative weights is inherently political.

nominations.contribution: for the axiomatic approach to fair division, mechanism design, and cooperative games
key_works: Moulin, 1988: Axioms of Cooperative Decision Making, Cambridge University Press
nominations.rationale: His focus on how specific rules and procedures guarantee impartial and fair outcomes is highly relevant for the design of bureaucratic and administrative systems. The mathematical precision is unimpeachable, though it largely abstracts away from the messy realities of political accountability and historical context.

nominations.contribution: for the theoretical and empirical foundations of comprehensive wealth measurement and sustainable development
key_works: Arrow, Dasgupta, et al., 2004: Are We Consuming Too Much?, Journal of Economic Perspectives
nominations.rationale: By integrating natural and social capital into national accounts, he provides a durable framework for long-run historical and comparative analysis. This expanded measurement of state assets is vital for evaluating long-term governance, even if pricing non-market institutions involves significant measurement error.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of bounded rationality and its implications for equilibrium theory
key_works: Rubinstein, 1998: Modeling Bounded Rationality, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: By relaxing the strict assumptions of perfect rationality, his work provides a more realistic foundation for how actors behave within institutional rules. The formal rigor ensures conceptual clarity, though bridging these abstract equilibrium models with large-N comparative political data remains a distant goal.

nominations.contribution: for her contributions to recursive methods in economic dynamics and their application to macroeconomic theory
key_works: Stokey, Lucas, and Prescott, 1989: Recursive Methods in Economic Dynamics, Harvard University Press
nominations.rationale: She co-developed the definitive toolkit for dynamic programming and recursive competitive equilibrium that underpins all of modern quantitative macroeconomics. These methodological breakthroughs made complex, infinite-horizon general-equilibrium problems mathematically rigorous and computationally solvable. It is arguably the most important methodological contribution to dynamic economics of the last forty years.

nominations.contribution: for their contributions to the theory of general equilibrium with incomplete markets
key_works: Geanakoplos and Polemarchakis, 1986: Existence, Regularity, and Constrained Suboptimality of Competitive Allocations when the Asset Market Is Incomplete, Essays in Honor of K. J. Arrow
nominations.rationale: They formalized the general equilibrium properties of incomplete markets, establishing the foundational result of constrained suboptimality. This theory proves that when markets are incomplete, aggregate pecuniary externalities mean that government intervention can Pareto-improve welfare. This is the theoretical bedrock upon which all heterogeneous-agent macroeconomics rests.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to welfare economics, population ethics, and the measurement of sustainable well-being
key_works: Dasgupta, 2001: Human Well-Being and the Natural Environment, Oxford University Press
nominations.rationale: He constructed a rigorous, theoretically consistent framework for comprehensive wealth accounting that incorporates environmental capital and intergenerational equity. His work disciplines long-run climate and environmental macro models by linking dynamic welfare functions directly to physical constraints. It is an exemplary fusion of normative theory and macroeconomic resource constraints.

nominations.contribution: for his contributions to welfare economics and the theory of fair allocation
key_works: Varian, 1974: Equity, Envy, and Efficiency, Journal of Economic Theory
nominations.rationale: He formalized the concept of envy-free allocations, providing a tractable and mathematically precise criterion for assessing equity in general equilibrium. This work allows economists to evaluate distributional consequences without relying entirely on ad hoc social welfare functions. It is a durable conceptual tool for normative economics.

nominations.contribution: for his foundational work on the integration of ethical principles into welfare economics and inequality measurement
key_works: Fleurbaey, 2008: Fairness, Responsibility, and Welfare, Oxford University Press
nominations.rationale: He has rigorously integrated concepts of individual responsibility and fairness into the formal mathematical apparatus of welfare economics. This allows models with heterogeneous agents to conduct principled, disciplined welfare counterfactuals that distinguish between inequality arising from luck versus choice. It deepens our ability to evaluate the true distributional consequences of macroeconomic policies.
